contracts.name: Badge
contracts.summary: A small label that shows the status or category of something.
useWhen: Showing a status in a table cell or card (Published, Draft…).
Labelling a category or count next to an item.

dontUseWhen.case: Something people can click to filter or remove

anatomy.description: Icon slot (Lucide, 12px), instead of the dot.

modifiers.description: Purple. Categories only, no status meaning.
Strong solid fill, for high emphasis.

a11y: Never show status by colour alone: always include .gds-badge__label text.
The dot and icon are decorative; the label carries the meaning.

rules.rule: Content status mapping: Published → positive, Draft → neutral, Scheduled → warning, Archived → neutral.
rules.why: Design decision (11 Nov 2026). Scheduled changes state on its own, so it draws attention; Draft and Archived need no action.

rules.rule: Status badges use the dot + label form.
rules.why: Status is not shown by colour alone.

rules.rule: A badge has exactly one colour variant.
rules.why: Two variants on one badge produce an undefined colour.

rules.rule: A badge is never a button or link.
rules.why: Badges have no hover or focus styles.

knownIssues.issue: Without a variant class the badge has no defined colour.
knownIssues.fix: v3: neutral by default, so the variant becomes optional.

contracts.name: Checkbox
contracts.summary: Lets people turn one option on or off, or pick several options from a list.
useWhen: Choosing any number of options from a short list.
Agreeing to something before submitting a form.

dontUseWhen.case: A setting that takes effect immediately
Exactly one choice from a list

anatomy.description: Wrapper. A <label>, so clicking the text toggles the box.
Native checkbox, visually hidden but focusable. Its :checked state drives the visual.

attributes.aria-label: Required when there is no visible label (e.g. in table cells)

anatomy.description: The visible box. Must come after the input (CSS uses the ~ sibling selector). Contains the icon: , or "minus" for mixed.

modifiers.description: Forces the checked look. Prefer the native checked attribute, which works without this class.
Indeterminate (some, not all, selected). Use the minus icon and set input.indeterminate = true in JS.
Disabled look. Also set the disabled attribute on the input.

states.name: disabled
states.how: gds-checkbox--disabled + disabled attribute on the input.

states.name: focus
states.how: Native :focus-visible on the input shows a ring on the control.

a11y: Keep the native input: it is what keyboards and screen readers use.
Without visible text, give the input an aria-label ("Select all", "Select <row name>").
For disabled, set the disabled attribute, not only the class.

rules.rule: Every .gds-checkbox contains an <input type="checkbox" class="gds-checkbox__input"> before .gds-checkbox__control.
rules.why: The visual state comes from the input through the ~ selector; without it the box never changes.

rules.rule: A checkbox without .gds-checkbox__label has an aria-label on the input.
rules.why: Otherwise it is announced as an unnamed checkbox.

rules.rule: The control contains the Lucide check icon (or minus for mixed). Do not draw your own SVG.
rules.why: Both AI tests drew their own tick because the guide showed <svg>...</svg>.

rules.rule: Checkboxes in table cells use gds-checkbox--sm.
rules.why: Matches the 16px icon grid of table rows.

knownIssues.issue: Checked can be shown two ways (native checked or gds-checkbox--checked), which can disagree.
knownIssues.fix: v3: drive the look only from the native state; keep --checked for docs previews.

examples.name: With label
In a table cell (no visible label)
Mixed (select all, some rows selected)

contracts.name: Dropdown
contracts.summary: A trigger that opens a panel of options: single select, multi-select, searchable lists.
useWhen: Choosing one or several values from a list (status filter, content type, author).
Lists long enough to need search.

dontUseWhen.case: 2–4 options that should all stay visible
Actions rather than values (Edit, Duplicate, Delete)

anatomy.description: Wrapper. Has no styles of its own: the product positions the panel (e.g. position: relative on the wrapper, absolute on the panel).
The floating panel. Hidden until gds-dropdown--open.

attributes.role: listbox (or contains the list with role=listbox)

anatomy.description: Search row at the top of the panel.
One option. A <button>, so it is focusable.
Rich items: stacks label and description.
Small count or status on the right.
Check icon, visible on the selected item (single select).

modifiers.description: Shows the panel and rotates the arrow. Set aria-expanded="true" on the trigger.

states.name: open
states.how: gds-dropdown--open on the wrapper + aria-expanded="true" on the trigger.

states.name: empty / loading
states.how: Show __empty or __loading inside the panel instead of the list.

a11y: Trigger: <button> with aria-haspopup="listbox" and aria-expanded.
Items: <button> elements (focusable), role="option", aria-selected.
Escape closes the panel and returns focus to the trigger (product JS).
Arrow keys move between items (product JS).

rules.rule: .gds-dropdown__item is a <button>, never a <li> or <div>.
rules.why: Non-button items cannot be reached with the keyboard; this was an unadmitted guess in the first AI test.

rules.rule: The trigger has aria-haspopup and aria-expanded matching gds-dropdown--open.
rules.why: Screen readers announce whether the list is open.

rules.rule: Next to a gds-input--md, use the default trigger size; next to --sm use __trigger--sm. Heights still differ slightly today (known issue).
rules.why: Closest available match; in the second AI test the filters were noticeably shorter than the search box.
rules.removeInV3: Align trigger heights to the input sizes (sm 32 / md 40 / lg 48) with matching modifier names.

rules.rule: Use dropdown for choosing values, menu for actions.
rules.why: Different semantics (listbox vs menu).

internal.why: Only used by the table action cell (with .is-open). Not part of the dropdown API; use __panel.

knownIssues.issue: .gds-dropdown has no CSS, so the panel is not positioned; docs examples use inline styles.
knownIssues.fix: v3: .gds-dropdown { position: relative } and an absolutely positioned panel by default.

knownIssues.issue: .gds-dropdown__menu exists only for the table action cell and is not part of this API.
Trigger heights do not match input heights.

contracts.name: Input
contracts.summary: A text field with optional label, icon, prefix/suffix, helper text and character count.
useWhen: Short free text: names, titles, emails, search.

dontUseWhen.case: Choosing from a known list of options

anatomy.description: Wrapper that stacks label, field and helper. Always has a size modifier.
Visible label. Link it with for/id.
The bordered box. Its height comes from the size modifier.
Fixed text before the value (e.g. https://).

attributes.aria-label: Required when there is no visible label (e.g. a search box)

anatomy.description: Helper or error text under the box.

modifiers.description: Red border. Put the message in __helper and set aria-invalid="true".
Disabled look. Also set disabled on the field.
Shadow instead of an outline border.

states.name: focus
states.how: Native :focus on the field highlights the wrap.

states.name: error
states.how: gds-input--error + message in __helper + aria-invalid="true" + aria-describedby pointing at the helper.

a11y: Every field has a name: a <label for> or, for search boxes, aria-label.
Placeholder is not a label.
Link helper and error text with aria-describedby.

rules.rule: Every .gds-input has exactly one of --sm, --md, --lg.
rules.why: The height lives on the size class; a bare .gds-input collapses.
rules.removeInV3: Give .gds-input the md height by default, so the size class becomes optional.

rules.rule: Every .gds-input__field has a linked <label> or an aria-label.
rules.why: An unnamed field is announced as "edit text".

rules.rule: --error always comes with a text message in __helper.
rules.why: A red border alone does not say what is wrong.

rules.rule: The field sits inside .gds-input__wrap, never directly in .gds-input.
rules.why: The border, icon and prefix layout live on the wrap.

knownIssues.issue: Older guides called --md the default although a bare .gds-input has no height.

contracts.name: Pagination
contracts.summary: Moves through pages of a long list, with an optional summary and page-size control.
useWhen: Below a table or list that has more records than fit on one page.

dontUseWhen.case: A feed people scroll through without needing a position
dontUseWhen.use: load more / infinite scroll (not in GDS yet)
tabs or a stepper (not in GDS yet)

anatomy.description: Bar around the page numbers. Under a table, always use it with --full.
Groups the page-size control and the page numbers on the right.
Page-size trigger: 10 Items per page + chevron-down icon. Not a native
Vertical separator between groups inside the bar. Not needed in the --full bar.
Row of page buttons. Page items are direct children; never a <ul>/<li> list.
A page number, or an arrow with --icon-only.
Labelled "Previous" / "Next" text button. Only for buttons with visible text; arrow-only buttons use __item--icon-only.

modifiers.description: Previous/next at the first or last page. Also set the disabled attribute.
Full-width bar with summary on the left. The one to use below tables.
Drops the border of the full bar (e.g. inside a card).
White pill bar for coloured backgrounds.

states.name: single page
states.how: Hide the number row when there is 1 page or less; keep the summary.

a11y: The <nav> has aria-label="Pagination".
The current page has aria-current="page".
Arrow-only buttons have aria-label ("Previous page", "Next page", "First page", "Last page").
Keyboard: ← → move one page, Home/End jump to first/last (implemented in JS by the product).

rules.rule: Page items are <button> elements directly inside <nav class="gds-pagination">; never <ul>/<li>.
rules.why: GDS has no CSS reset, so list bullets and padding show.
rules.removeInV3: Reset list styles inside .gds-pagination so a list also renders correctly.

rules.rule: Below a table use .gds-pagination-bar.gds-pagination-bar--full.
rules.why: One consistent paging bar for lists.

rules.rule: The page-size control is .gds-pagination-bar__select (a button), not a native <select>.
rules.why: A native select does not match the bar and was a wrong guess in the first AI test.

rules.rule: __nav is only for buttons with visible "Previous"/"Next" text; arrow-only buttons use __item--icon-only with aria-label.
rules.why: The two have different sizes and spacing.

rules.rule: Exactly one item is --current and it has aria-current="page".
rules.why: Position must not be visual only.

internal.why: Docs preview that forces the hover look.
Docs preview that forces the focus ring.

knownIssues.issue: The page-size menu has no GDS markup of its own; docs use a .gds-menu positioned by script.
knownIssues.fix: v3: document the page-size menu as part of this contract, or reuse dropdown.

contracts.name: Data table
contracts.summary: Rows of records with optional selection, sorting, bulk actions and pagination.
useWhen: Showing many records that share the same fields (entries, assets, users, orders).
People need to compare, sort, select or act on several records at once.

dontUseWhen.case: Fewer than about 5 records with no comparison needed
Key/value details of a single record
dontUseWhen.use: a description list inside a card

anatomy.description: Bulk-action bar. Sibling placed directly above .gds-table. Hidden until is-visible is added.
Vertical separator between count and actions.
Optional wrapper for horizontal scroll. Wraps .gds-table.

attributes.aria-label: Name of the data, unless a <caption> is used

anatomy.description: One cell. Header cells are <th scope="col">.
Wraps the sort icon inside a sortable header cell. Unsorted: arrow-up-down; sorted: arrow-up (CSS flips it for descending).
Flex wrapper for icon + text combinations inside a cell.
Entry cell layout: thumbnail + title + subtitle (mainly in the cards variant).

attributes.alt: Describe the image, or "" if decorative

anatomy.description: Secondary text, e.g. slug or path.
Row overflow (⋯) button in the action cell.
Empty-state message, inside a single full-width cell (colspan) in the body.
Loading placeholder bar inside a cell, used with gds-table--loading.

modifiers.description: Each row is a separate card with shadow and gap.
Below the mobile breakpoint, rows stack as label/value pairs. Each <td> needs data-label.
Loading state with skeleton rows. Add aria-busy="true" on the <table>.
Narrow rightmost cell holding the row overflow button.
Lighter, smaller text for dates and metadata columns.
Header text for an action column (e.g. "Edit").
Header cell that can be sorted. Shows the sort icon.
The active sort column (highlights the icon). Required for both directions.
Descending. Added on top of --sorted; rotates the arrow-up icon 180°.
Freezes the checkbox column during horizontal scroll.
Freezes the entry (second) column during horizontal scroll.

states.name: hover
states.how: Native :hover on body rows. No class needed.

states.name: selected
states.how: gds-table__row--selected on the row, plus a checked .gds-checkbox in its checkbox cell.

states.name: loading
states.how: gds-table--loading on the container, aria-busy="true" on the table, skeleton bars in cells.

states.name: empty
states.how: One body row with a single cell (colspan = column count) containing .gds-table__empty.

a11y: Name the table with aria-label on <table> or a <caption>.
Every header cell is <th scope="col">.
The sorted header has aria-sort="ascending" or "descending"; others have none.
Sortable headers are not keyboard-reachable yet: GDS has no styled sort button. Flag this gap; do not add an unstyled <button>.
The select-all checkbox has aria-label="Select all"; each row checkbox has aria-label="Select <row name>".
Header text uses --table-header-color (text-label, 8.50:1).

rules.rule: The root class is gds-table. There is no gds-data-table class.
rules.why: AI tools often guess gds-data-table from the component name.

rules.rule: Every <th> has scope="col".
rules.why: Screen readers announce the column for each cell.

rules.rule: The <table> has aria-label or a <caption>.
rules.why: A table without a name is announced only as "table".

rules.rule: A descending column has both --sorted and --sorted-desc, and uses the arrow-up icon.
rules.why: --sorted-desc rotates the icon; arrow-down would point up. Without --sorted the icon is not highlighted.
rules.removeInV3: One modifier per direction: --sort-asc / --sort-desc, each picking its own icon.

rules.rule: The sorted <th> has aria-sort matching the direction.
rules.why: Sort state must not be visual only.

rules.rule: Every checkbox inside the table has an aria-label.
rules.why: Checkboxes in cells have no visible label.

rules.rule: Status cells use .gds-badge with dot + label, following the content-status mapping in the badge contract.
rules.why: One status language across products; status is never colour alone.

rules.rule: Paging below a table uses .gds-pagination-bar--full, never custom markup.
rules.why: Custom pagination was the most broken part of the first AI test.

rules.rule: The bulk-action bar sits directly above .gds-table (or .gds-table-scroll) and is shown with is-visible only while rows are selected.
rules.why: Consistent place for bulk actions.
rules.removeInV3: Rename is-visible to gds-table__toolbar--visible (BEM, no exception).

rules.rule: Cell content composes GDS components (checkbox, avatar-name, badge, button). Do not build one-off cell UI.
rules.why: Keeps tables consistent and themeable.

internal.why: Docs preview that forces the hover look. Real hover is native :hover.
Docs preview that forces a striped row. Use gds-table--striped.
Docs-only cell that labels demo rows ("Default", "Hovered").

knownIssues.issue: Sortable header cells are clickable only with a mouse; there is no styled button element for keyboard users.
knownIssues.fix: v3: a gds-table__sort-btn element (reset button inside <th>) so sorting works with Tab + Enter.

knownIssues.issue: The action-cell dropdown uses .gds-dropdown__menu and .is-open, while the Dropdown component uses .gds-dropdown__panel and .gds-dropdown--open.
is-visible on the toolbar breaks the BEM naming rule.
Sorting needs two modifiers and one specific icon.
GDS has no page header or filter bar yet. Until it does, follow Critical Rule 9 (layout-only CSS with a product prefix and GDS tokens, marked /* GDS gap */).
knownIssues.fix: v3 patterns: Page header, Filter bar, List page.
